questions.stem: A lipid-soluble drug undergoes a phase I reaction followed by glucuronidation. Compared with the parent drug, the final glucuronide conjugate is most likely:

options.A: More lipid-soluble and reabsorbed in the renal tubule
options.B: Polar, pharmacologically inactive, and excreted in bile or urine
options.C: Chemically reactive and potentially toxic or carcinogenic
options.D: More pharmacologically active than the parent drug
options.E: Stored in body fat until it is metabolized further

questions.explanation: Phase II conjugates are almost always inactive, highly water-soluble, and excreted in bile (> 300 Da) or urine (< 300 Da). A: Both phases decrease lipid solubility, which limits tubular reabsorption. C: Chemically reactive, possibly toxic products are typical of phase I. D: Active metabolites arise mainly from phase I (e.g., codeine → morphine); phase II products are usually inactive. E: Polar conjugates don't accumulate in fat.

questions.stem: Which reaction is a phase II metabolic reaction?
questions.explanation: Acetylation is a conjugation (synthetic) reaction, as are glucuronidation, sulfation, methylation, and glutathione/glycine conjugation. B: Oxidation is phase I (functionalization). C: Hydrolysis is phase I. D: Reduction is phase I. E: Deamination is phase I.

questions.stem: A patient stable on warfarin is started on rifampin for tuberculosis. Two weeks later the INR has fallen below target. What is the mechanism?

options.D: Increased vitamin K synthesis by gut flora
options.E: Induction of hepatic enzymes that metabolize warfarin

questions.explanation: Rifampin is a classic inducer: more microsomal enzyme → faster warfarin clearance → lower levels and INR over time. A: Inhibition would raise the INR. B: Displacement would transiently raise free warfarin and the INR. C: Rifampin doesn't meaningfully block warfarin absorption. D: Not the mechanism of this interaction.

questions.stem: Grapefruit juice markedly raises blood levels of oral felodipine but not of IV felodipine. What explains the difference?
questions.explanation: Grapefruit blocks CYP3A4 in the gut wall, so only orally given drug escapes presystemic metabolism. A: The wrong isoform and site. B: Induction of renal P-gp would lower levels, not raise them. C: Protein displacement wouldn't depend on the route. E: Glucuronidation doesn't happen in plasma and isn't the mechanism.

questions.stem: A patient taking lovastatin develops muscle pain a week after starting erythromycin. Which mechanism best explains this?
questions.explanation: Statins are CYP3A4 substrates ("3A4 SICS"); erythromycin inhibits their metabolism → ↑ statin levels → muscle toxicity. A: Induction would lower statin levels. B: CYP2C9 handles warfarin, NSAIDs and sulfonylureas. C: CYP2D6 handles codeine, antidepressants, tamoxifen and β-blockers. E: CYP2C19 handles PPIs and phenytoin (and clopidogrel, outside the slides).

questions.stem: An 80-year-old taking diazepam nightly becomes increasingly drowsy over several weeks at the same dose. Which combination of age-related changes best explains this?

options.A: ↓ hepatic microsomal activity and ↑ Vd of lipid-soluble drugs

questions.explanation: Aging reduces microsomal (phase I) activity and increases Vd of lipophilic drugs (more fat), so diazepam accumulates with repeated doses. B: Both changes go the other way. C: Diazepam is lipophilic and not cleared unchanged by the kidney; renal function also declines with age. D: Lower absorption would reduce drowsiness. E: More conjugation would speed clearance.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man has a coronary stent placed and is discharged on clopidogrel. His primary physician adds omeprazole for dyspepsia. Months later he has stent thrombosis. Which mechanism most likely contributed?

options.A: Omeprazole induced CYP3A4, accelerating clopidogrel clearance
options.C: Omeprazole raised gastric pH, preventing clopidogrel absorption
options.D: Omeprazole inhibited CYP2C19, reducing activation of clopidogrel

questions.explanation: Clopidogrel is a prodrug activated by CYP2C19; omeprazole inhibits CYP2C19 → less active metabolite → weaker platelet inhibition. A: Omeprazole isn't a meaningful CYP3A4 inducer here. B: Displacement wouldn't reduce antiplatelet effect long-term. C: The interaction is metabolic, not absorption-based. E: The P2Y12 receptor is clopidogrel's target, not omeprazole's.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man with chronic heavy alcohol use takes regular therapeutic doses of acetaminophen for a week and develops liver injury. What best explains his susceptibility?

options.A: Alcohol inhibits acetaminophen metabolism, so the parent drug accumulates
options.C: Alcohol increases glucuronidation, making inactive conjugates
options.D: Alcohol decreases the Vd of acetaminophen
options.E: Alcohol induces microsomal enzymes, increasing toxic NAPQI formation

questions.explanation: Chronic alcohol induces microsomal enzymes; acetaminophen is toxified to NAPQI, so induction increases toxicity (the lecture's alcohol → acetaminophen → liver toxicity example). A: Inhibition by chronic alcohol isn't the mechanism, and the parent drug isn't the hepatotoxin. B: Protein displacement doesn't create a toxic metabolite. C: More inactive conjugates would be protective. D: A Vd change doesn't explain hepatotoxicity.

questions.stem: A 50-year-old woman taking fluoxetine, a CYP2D6 inhibitor, gets almost no pain relief from codeine after a dental extraction. What best explains this?

options.A: Fluoxetine induces codeine metabolism to inactive products
options.B: Fluoxetine displaces codeine from plasma proteins
options.C: Reduced conversion of codeine to morphine, its active metabolite
options.D: Codeine accumulates as the parent drug and blocks opioid receptors
options.E: Fluoxetine inhibits phase II glucuronidation of codeine

questions.explanation: Codeine is converted by CYP2D6 to morphine, which provides the analgesia; inhibiting CYP2D6 reduces this activation. A: Fluoxetine is an inhibitor, not an inducer. B: Displacement would increase free drug, not reduce its effect. D: Codeine isn't a receptor blocker; higher parent levels don't explain lost analgesia. E: Glucuronidation inactivates drugs; inhibiting it wouldn't reduce activation.

questions.stem: Morphine, which is excreted mainly as a glucuronide, is not used as an analgesic during labor. What is the reason?

options.A: Neonatal enzymes are immature, so morphine is cleared slowly
options.B: Neonates have higher CYP3A4 activity, producing toxic metabolites
options.C: Morphine is a prodrug activated only in the fetal liver
options.D: The placenta metabolizes morphine to an active toxin

questions.explanation: Several enzymes have low activity in neonates (especially premature ones) and need at least 8 weeks to reach adult levels, so morphine that crosses to the baby isn't cleared. B: Neonatal enzyme activity is lower, not higher. C: Morphine is already active; codeine is the prodrug example. D: The issue is neonatal clearance, not placental toxification. E: Binding isn't the reason given; reduced metabolism is.
